edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: These exposures act mainly through renal sodium handling, vascular smooth-muscle tone, and neurohormonal blood-pressure regulation. That makes them particularly relevant to Blood pressure control when salt sensitivity, baseline blood pressure, or medication use already place the system under stress.
edges.summary: Sodium reduction appears tied to better blood pressure control in general adult mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
